summary: Iteration 12: End-to-end testing of EasyBillsPay v2 billing smoothing engine + subscription pricing layer. Backend: 13/13 pytest cases PASS for all /api/v2/* endpoints (predict-bills, simulate-plan, plan-health, savings-comparison, subscription/tiers, subscription/current, subscription/select). Frontend: all spec items verified via Playwright — sidebar nav shows new 'Annual Plan' + 'Subscription' items, /dashboard/forecast renders title 'Your Annual Plan' with stats ($324.49/mo smoothed, $3605.49 annual predicted, peak Jul 2026, $77.42 variance), plan-health-card, Recharts forecast-chart, savings-summary (95% vs 100% predictability), category-forecast (Internet/Electricity/Gas/Water). Frequency toggles correctly change smoothed amount (Weekly $74.88 / Fortnightly $149.77 / Monthly $324.49). /dashboard/subscription shows 3 tier cards with correct pricing (Free / $9.90 / $19.90), 'Current Plan' state works after select. Existing flows (Overview, Bill Intelligence, Payment Plan, Login) all intact.
critical_code_review_comments: billing_engine.predict_annual_bills assumes monthly frequency when bill.frequency is missing/unknown via _annualize default — fine but log a warning when an unknown freq is encountered for observability.
_offset_month clamps day to 28 which is safe for month math but causes the month label to always be on day-28 of the source month; only month/year are surfaced in UI so no visible impact.

/api/v2/simulate-plan filters bills by status='pending' while predict-bills and savings-comparison use ALL bills. This is inconsistent — a user with bills all marked 'paid' would see a forecast but no simulation. Document intent or unify.
/api/v2/subscription/select takes 'tier' as a query string param on a POST — acceptable but a JSON body { tier } is more conventional and easier to validate via Pydantic.
Buffer percentage is read from SUBSCRIPTION_TIERS but the tier's buffer value (5/8) is duplicated in three endpoints; consider a single helper get_user_buffer(user_id).

ForecastDashboard.jsx fires three sequential requests (predict-bills, simulate-plan, savings-comparison, plan-health) on every freq toggle. Consider memoising predict-bills/savings-comparison since only simulate-plan depends on frequency.
SubscriptionTiers.jsx selectTier does not show a toast on failure (only re-throws); user-facing error UX is silent.

No tier-gating yet enforced on /api/v2/* endpoints — a 'basic' user can still hit forecasting endpoints (which the tier features list claims are Standard+). If tier-gating is intended, enforce it server-side.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing 17 seeded bills across Electricity/Water/Internet/Gas. Subscription test resets user tier to 'basic' at the end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: v2 billing smoothing + subscription tiers are production-ready. Backend endpoints respond in <1s (no GPT calls). Pytest file at /app/backend/tests/test_v2_billing_smoothing.py covers: 12-month forecast shape, seasonal variation, auth gating, frequency-based per-period amount differences, invalid frequency 400, plan-health response shape, savings-comparison shape, 3-tier list with correct pricing ($0/$9.90/$19.90), default 'basic', tier select persistence, invalid tier 400, and premium-vs-basic buffer difference (5% vs 8% reflected in smoothed_amount). Frontend data-testids verified: forecast-dashboard, forecast-title, stat-smoothed-amount, stat-annual-predicted, stat-peak-month, stat-variance, plan-health-card, forecast-chart, savings-summary, category-forecast, freq-weekly/fortnightly/monthly, subscription-tiers, tiers-title, tier-basic/standard/premium, select-tier-basic/standard/premium, nav-annual-plan, nav-subscription.
